paragraphs: Hackney Council's fostering service looks after the borough's own children in care, and the services shown above also take enquiries from people living in Hackney. In May 2024 the council said it had almost 400 children in care but only 130 approved foster carers, that its mainstream fostering households had fallen for a second year in a row, and that approvals of new carers were down 41% on the year before. Its deputy mayor warned that more children were at risk of being placed outside the borough. The council aims to approve at least 20 new foster carers every year.

The placements Hackney says it most needs are for children aged 4 to 12, teenagers aged 13 to 16, sibling groups and disabled children, along with its specialist teenage and parent and child schemes. Carers can offer emergency, short-term, long-term or respite care of up to 21 days.

You need to be over 21, in good health, with time to foster and a secure home with a spare bedroom, which you do not need to own. Hackney welcomes single people, couples of any kind including same-sex couples, people who work full time or not at all, and people past retirement age. You can live outside the borough as long as you can travel to Hackney for training and groups. Everyone is DBS checked, and a conviction does not rule you out automatically. Skills to Foster training comes before the assessment.

For its own carers, Hackney lists a dedicated social worker, an out-of-hours phone line, a fortnightly therapeutic support group and a men's group, clinical support, the Virtual School, a quarterly carers' forum, buddying, and free membership of the Fostering Network and, for LGBTQ+ carers, New Family Social. Its carers also qualify for help with council tax. Hackney is one of six councils, with Barnet, Camden, Enfield, Haringey and Islington, in the North London Fostering Hub hosted by Camden, which grew from a consortium the six have shared since 2012.

Speak to the council and to two or three of the services above before you decide. If you live near the borough's edge, see our pages for Islington, Haringey, Tower Hamlets and Newham, or East London and London as a whole.
